1.1: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim, and the Word was Elohim.
1.2: He was in the beginning with Elohim.
1.3: All came to be through Him, and without Him not even one came to be that came to be.
1.4: In Him was Ḥai, and the Ḥai was the Light of men.
1.5: And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
1.6: There was a man sent from Elohim, whose name was Yoḥanan.
1.7: This one came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light, that all might believe through him.
1.8: He was not that Light, but that he might bear witness of that Light.
1.9: He was the true Light, which enlightens every man, coming into the world.
1.10: He was in the world, and the world came to be through Him, and the world did not know Him.
1.11: He came to His own, and His own did not receive Him.
1.12: But as many as received Him, to them He gave the authority to become children of Elohim, to those believing in His Name,
1.13: who were born, not of blood nor of the desire of flesh nor of the desire of man, but of Elohim.
1.14: And the Word became flesh and pitched His tent among us, and we saw His esteem, esteem as of an only brought-forth of a father, complete in favor and truth.
1.15: Yoḥanan bore witness of Him and cried out, saying, “This was He of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has become before me, because He was before me.’ ”
1.16: And out of His completeness we all received, and favor upon favor,
1.17: for the Torah was given through Mosheh - the favor and the truth came through 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 Mashiaḥ.
1.18: No one has ever seen Elohim. The only brought-forth Bĕn, who is in the bosom of the Father, He declared.
1.19: Now this was the witness of Yoḥanan when the Yahuḏim sent from Yerushalayim kohenim and Lĕwites to ask him, “Who are you?”
1.20: And he confessed, and did not deny, but confessed, “I am not ha’Mashiaḥ.”
1.21: And they asked him, “What then? Are you Ĕliyahu?” So he said, “I am not.” “Are you the Naḇi?” And he answered, “No.”
1.22: Therefore they said to him, “Who are you, so that we give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say about yourself?”
1.23: He said, “I am a voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,’ as the naḇi Yeshayahu said.”
1.24: And those sent were of the Pharisees,
1.25: and they asked him, saying, “Why then do you immerse if you are not ha’Mashiaḥ, nor Ĕliyahu, nor the Naḇi?”
1.26: Yoḥanan answered them, saying, “I immerse in water, but in your midst stands One whom you do not know,
1.27: the One coming after me, who has become before me, whose sandal strap l am not worthy to loosen.”
1.28: This took place in Bĕyth Aḇarah beyond the Yardĕn, where Yoḥanan was immersing.
1.29: On the next day Yoḥanan saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 coming toward him, and said, “See, the Lamb of Elohim who takes away the sin of the world!
1.30: “This is He of whom I said, ‘After me comes a Man who has become before me, for He was before me.’
1.31: “And l did not know Him, but that He might be revealed to Yisra’ĕl, therefore I came immersing in water.”
1.32: And Yoḥanan bore witness, saying, “I have seen the Ruaḥ coming down from the shamayim like a dove and remain on Him.
1.33: “And I did not know Him, but He who sent me to immerse in water said to me, ‘Upon whom you see the Ruaḥ coming down and remaining on Him, this is He who immerses in the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh.’
1.34: “And I have seen and have witnessed that this is the Bĕn of Elohim.”
1.35: Again the following day, Yoḥanan was standing with two of his talmidim,
1.36: and looking at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 walking, he said, “See the Lamb of Elohim!”
1.37: And the two talmidim heard him speaking, and they followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
1.38: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 turning, and seeing them following, said to them, “What do you seek?” And they said to Him, “Rabbi,” which translated means, Teacher, “where are You staying?”
1.39: He said to them, “Come and see.” They went and saw where He was staying, and remained with Him that day. Now it was about the tenth hour.
1.40: Andri, the brother of Shim’on Kĕpha, was one of the two who heard from Yoḥanan, and followed Him.
1.41: First he found his own brother Shim’on, and said to him, “We have found ha’Mashiaḥ,” which interpreted is, the Anointed.
1.42: And he brought him to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏. And looking at him, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said, “You are Shim’on the son of Yonah, you shall be called Kĕpha,” which translated is, a stone.
1.43: On the following day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 wanted to go to Galil, and He found Philippos and said to him, “Follow Me.”
1.44: And Philippos was from Bĕyth Tsaiḏa, the city of Andri and Kĕpha.
1.45: Philippos found Nethan’ĕl and said to him, “We have found Him whom Mosheh wrote of in the Torah, and the Neḇi’im: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 of Natsareth - the son of Yosĕph.”
1.46: And Nethan’ĕl said to him, “Is it possible for any good to come out of Natsareth?” Philippos said to him, “Come and see.”
1.47: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 saw Nethan’ĕl coming toward Him, and said of him, “See, truly a Yisra’ĕlite, in whom is no deceit!”
1.48: Nethan’ĕl said to Him, “From where do You know me?” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered and said to him, “Before Philippos called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.”
1.49: Nethan’ĕl answered and said to Him, “Rabbi, You are the Bĕn of Elohim! You are the Meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl!”
1.50: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered and said to him, “Because I said to you, ‘I saw you under the fig tree,’ do you believe? Greater than that you shall see.”
1.51: And He said to him, “Truly, truly, I say to you, from now on you shall see the shamayim opened, and the messengers of Elohim ascending and descending upon the Bĕn of Aḏam.”

10.1: “Truly, truly, I say to you, he who does not enter through the door into the sheepfold, but climbs up by another way, that one is a thief and a robber.
10.2: “But he who enters through the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
10.3: “The doorkeeper opens for him, and the sheep hear his voice. And he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
10.4: “And when he has brought out his own sheep, he goes before them. And the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.
10.5: “And they shall by no means follow a stranger, but shall flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers.”
10.6: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 used this figure of speech, but they did not know what He had been saying to them.
10.7: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 therefore said to them again, “Truly, truly, I say to you, I am the door of the sheep.
10.8: “All who came before Me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not hear them.
10.9: “I am the door. Whoever enters through Me, he shall be saved, and shall go in and shall go out and find pasture.
10.10: “The thief does not come except to steal, and to slaughter, and to destroy. I have come that they might possess ḥai, and that they might possess it beyond measure.
10.11: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down His ḥai for the sheep.
10.12: “But the hireling, and not being a shepherd - one who does not own the sheep - sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees. And the wolf snatches the sheep and scatters them.
10.13: “Now the hireling flees because he is a hireling and is not concerned about the sheep.
10.14: “I am the good shepherd. And I know Mine, and Mine know Me,
10.15: even as the Father knows Me, and I know the Father. And I lay down My ḥai for the sheep.
10.16: “And other sheep I have which are not of this fold - I have to bring them as well, and they shall hear My voice, and there shall be one flock, one Shepherd.
10.17: “Because of this the Father loves Me, because I lay down My ḥai, in order to receive it again.
10.18: “No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of Myself. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to receive it again. This command I have received from My Father.”
10.19: Again there came a division among the Yahuḏim because of these words,
10.20: and many of them said, “He has a demon and is mad, why do you listen to Him?”
10.21: Others said, “These are not the words of one possessed by a demon. Is a demon able to open the eyes of the blind?”
10.22: At that time the Ḥanukkah came to be in Yerushalayim, and it was winter.
10.23: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was walking in the Miqdash, in the porch of Shelomoh.
10.24: So the Yahuḏim surrounded Him and said to Him, “How long do You keep us in suspense? If You are ha’Mashiaḥ, say to us plainly.”
10.25: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered them, “I have told you, and you do not believe. The works that I do in My Father’s Name, they bear witness concerning Me.
10.26: “But you do not believe, because you are not of My sheep, as I said to you.
10.27: “My sheep hear My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me.
10.28: “And I give them everlasting ḥai, and they shall by no means ever perish, and no one shall snatch them out of My hand.
10.29: “My Father, who has given them to Me, is greater than all. And no one is able to snatch them out of My Father’s hand.
10.31: Again the Yahuḏim picked up stones to stone Him.
10.32: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered them, “Many good works I have shown you from My Father. For which of these works do you stone Me?”
10.33: The Yahuḏim answered Him, saying, “We do not stone You for a good work, but for blasphemy, and because You, being a Man, make Yourself Elohim.”
10.34: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered them, “Is it not written in your own Torah, ‘I said, “You are Elohim” ’?
10.35: “If He called them elohim, to whom the Word of Elohim came - and it is impossible for the Scripture to be broken -
10.36: do you say of Him whom the Father made qadosh and sent into the world, ‘You are blaspheming,’ because I said, ‘I am the Bĕn of Elohim’?
10.37: “If I do not do the works of My Father, do not believe Me;
10.38: but if I do, though you do not believe Me, believe the works, so that you know and believe that the Father is in Me, and I in Him.”
10.39: Therefore they were seeking again to seize Him, but He went forth out of their hand,
10.40: and went once more to the other side of the Yardĕn to the place where Yoḥanan was immersing at first, and there He stayed.
10.41: And many came to Him and said, “Yoḥanan indeed did no sign, yet all that Yoḥanan said about this Man was true.”
10.42: And many believed in Him there.

11.1: And a certain one was sick, El’azar from, Bĕyth Anyah, the village of Miryam and her sister Martha.
11.2: Now it was Miryam who anointed the Aḏon with perfume and wiped His feet with her hair, whose brother El’azar was sick.
11.3: Therefore the sisters sent to Him, saying, “Aḏonai, see, he whom You love is sick.”
11.4: But when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 heard, He said, “This sickness is not unto death, but for the esteem of Elohim, so that the Bĕn of Elohim might be esteemed by it.”
11.5: Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 loved Martha and her sister and El’azar.
11.6: Therefore, when He heard that he was sick, then indeed He stayed at the place where He was, two more days.
11.7: Then after this He said to the talmidim, “Let us go back to Yahuḏah.”
11.8: The talmidim said to Him, “Rabbi, the Yahuḏim were just now seeking to stone You, and are You going back there?”
11.9: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered, “Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
11.10: “But if anyone walks in the night, he stumbles, because the Light is not in him.”
11.11: He said this, and after that He said to them, “Our friend El’azar has fallen asleep, but I am going there, to wake him up.”
11.12: Therefore the talmidim said to Him, “Aḏonai, if he has fallen asleep he shall recover.”
11.13: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had spoken about his death, whereas they thought that He spoke of taking rest in sleep.
11.14: So then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them plainly, “El’azar has died.
11.15: “And for your sake I am glad I was not there, in order for you to believe. But let us go to him.”
11.16: T’oma, who is called the Twin, then said to his fellow talmidim, “Let us also go, so that we die with Him.”
11.17: Therefore, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 arrived, He found that he had already been four days in the tomb.
11.18: Now Bĕyth Anyah was near Yerushalayim, about fifteen stadion away.
11.19: And many of the Yahuḏim had come to Martha and Miryam, to comfort them concerning their brother.
11.20: Martha, then, when she heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was coming, met Him, but Miryam was sitting in the house.
11.21: Martha, then, said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, “Aḏonai, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.
11.22: “But even now I know that whatever You might ask of Elohim, Elohim shall give You.”
11.23: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “Your brother shall rise again.”
11.24: Martha said to Him, “I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”
11.25: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “I am the resurrection and the ḥai. He who believes in Me, though he dies, he shall live.
11.26: “And everyone that is living and believing in Me shall never die at all. Do you believe this?”
11.27: She said to Him, “Yes, Aḏonai, I believe that You are ha’Mashiaḥ, the Bĕn of Elohim, who is coming into the world.”
11.28: And having said this she went away and called her sister Miryam secretly, saying, “The Teacher is here and calls you.”
11.29: When she heard, she rose up quickly and came to Him.
11.30: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had not yet come into the village, but was in the place where Martha met Him.
11.31: Therefore the Yahuḏim who were with her in the house, and were comforting her, when they saw that Miryam rose up quickly and went out, followed her, saying, “She is going to the tomb to weep there.”
11.32: Miryam, therefore, when she came where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was, and saw Him, she fell down at His feet, saying to Him, “Aḏonai, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.”
11.33: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, therefore, when He saw her weeping, and the Yahuḏim who came with her weeping, He groaned in the spirit and was troubled,
11.34: and said, “Where have you laid him?” They said to Him, “Aḏonai, come and see.”
11.36: The Yahuḏim therefore said, “See how He loved him!”
11.37: And some of them said, “Was this One, who opened the eyes of the blind, not also able to prevent this one from dying?”
11.38: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, therefore, again groaning in Himself, came to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay against it.
11.39: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of him who had died, said to Him, “Aḏonai, already he smells, for it is four days.”
11.40: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “Did I not say to you that if you believe, you shall see the esteem of Elohim?”
11.41: So they took away the stone where the dead man was laid. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 lifted up His eyes and said, “Father, I thank You that You have heard Me.
11.42: “And I knew that You always hear Me, but because of the crowd standing by I said this, in order that they believe that You sent Me.”
11.43: And when He had said this, He cried with a loud voice, “El’azar, come out!”
11.44: And he who died came out bound feet and hands with wrappings, and his face was wrapped with a cloth. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Loosen him, and let him go.”
11.45: Therefore many of the Yahuḏim who had come to Miryam, and had seen what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 did, believed in Him.
11.46: But some of them went away to the Pharisees and told them what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 did.
11.47: So the chief kohenim and the Pharisees gathered a council and said, “What shall we do? Because this Man does many signs.
11.48: “If we let Him alone like this, they all shall believe in Him, and the Romans shall come and take away from us both our place and nation.”
11.49: And one of them, Qayapha, being kohĕn ha’gadol that year, said to them, “You know naught,
11.50: neither do you consider that it is better for us that one man die for the people than that the entire nation should perish.”
11.51: But he did not say this from himself, but being kohĕn ha’gadol that year he naḇu that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was about to die for the nation,
11.52: and not for the nation only, but to gather together into one the children of Elohim who were scattered abroad.
11.53: So from that day on they plotted to kill Him.
11.54: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 therefore no longer went openly among the Yahuḏim, but went from there into the country near the wilderness, to a city called Ephrayim, and remained there with His talmidim.
11.55: Now the Pesaḥ of the Yahuḏim was near, and many went from the country up to Yerushalayim before the Pesaḥ, to cleanse themselves.
11.56: And so they were seeking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, and spoke among one another, standing in the Miqdash, “What do you think? Is He not coming to the Festival at all?”
11.57: And both the chief kohenim and the Pharisees had given a command, that if anyone knew where He was, he should disclose it, in order for them to seize Him.

12.1: Accordingly 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, six days before the Pesaḥ, came to Bĕyth Anyah, where El’azar was, who had died, whom He raised from the dead.
12.2: So they made Him a supper there, and Martha served, while El’azar was one of those who sat at the table with Him.
12.3: Then Miryam took a litra of costly perfume of nard, anointed the feet of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, and wiped His feet with her hair. And the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
12.4: Then one of His talmidim, Yahuḏah from Qeriyoth, of Shim’on, who was about to deliver Him up, said,
12.5: “Why was this perfume not sold for three hundred pieces of silver and given to the poor?”
12.6: And he said this, not because he was concerned about the poor, but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and he used to take what was put in it.
12.7: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 then said, “Let her alone, she has kept this for the day of My burial.
12.8: “For the poor you have with you always, but Me you do not have always.”
12.9: Then a great crowd of the Yahuḏim learned that He was there. And they came, not on account of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 only, but also to see El’azar, whom He had raised from the dead.
12.10: And the chief kohenim resolved to kill El’azar as well,
12.11: because on account of him many of the Yahuḏim went away and believed in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
12.12: On the next day a great crowd who had come to the Festival, when they heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was coming to Yerushalayim,
12.13: took the branches of palm trees and went out to meet Him, and were crying out, “Hoshia-na! Baruḵ is He who is coming in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl!”
12.14: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, having found a young donkey, sat on it, as it has been written:
12.15: “Do not fear, daughter of Tsiyon, see, your Meleḵ is coming, sitting on the colt of a donkey.”
12.16: At first His talmidim did not understand this. But when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was esteemed, then they remembered that this was written about Him and that they had done this to Him.
12.17: Therefore the crowd, who were with Him when He called El’azar out of his tomb and raised him from the dead, were bearing witness.
12.18: On account of this the crowd also met Him, because they heard that He had done this sign.
12.19: The Pharisees then said among themselves, “You see how you are getting nowhere at all. Look, the world has gone after Him!”
12.20: And there were certain Yawanites among those coming up to worship at the Festival.
12.21: These then came to Philippos, who was from Bĕyth Tsaiḏa of Galil, and were asking him, saying, “Aḏonai, we want to see 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.”
12.22: Philippos came and told Andri, and in turn Andri and Philippos told 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
12.23: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered them, saying, “The hour has come for the Bĕn of Aḏam to be esteemed.
12.24: “Truly, truly, I say to you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it remains alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
12.25: “He who loves his life shall lose it, and he who hates his life in this world shall preserve it for everlasting ḥai.
12.26: “If anyone serves Me, let him follow Me. And where I am, there My servant also shall be. If anyone serves Me, the Father shall value him.
12.27: “Now I Myself am troubled, and what shall I say? ‘Father, save Me from this hour’? But for this reason I came to this hour.
12.28: “Father, esteem Your Name.” Then a voice came from the shamayim, “I have both esteemed it and shall esteem it again.”
12.29: So the crowd who stood by and heard it were saying there had been thunder. Others said, “A messenger has spoken to Him.”
12.30: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered and said, “This voice did not come because of Me, but for your sake.
12.31: “Now is the judgment of this world, now the ruler of this world shall be cast out.
12.32: “And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, shall draw all unto Myself.”
12.33: This He said, signifying by what death He was about to die.
12.34: The crowd answered Him, “We have heard out of the Torah that ha’Mashiaḥ remains forever. And how do You say, ‘The Bĕn of Aḏam has to be lifted up’? Who is this Bĕn of Aḏam?”
12.35: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, therefore, said to them, “Yet a little while the Light is with you. Walk while you have the Light, lest darkness overtake you. And he who walks in darkness does not know where he is going.
12.36: “While you have the Light, believe in the Light, so that you become sons of Light.” These 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 spoke, and went off and was hidden from them.
12.37: But though He had done so many signs before them, they did not believe in Him,
12.38: that the word of Yeshayahu the naḇi might be filled, which he spoke, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 been revealed?”
12.39: Because of this they were unable to believe, because again Yeshayahu said:
12.40: “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they should not see with their eyes and understand with their heart, and turn, and I should heal them.”
12.41: Yeshayahu said this when he saw His esteem and spoke of Him.
12.42: Still, even among the rulers many believed in Him, but because of the Pharisees they did not confess, lest they should be put out of the congregation,
12.43: for they loved the praise of men more than the praise of Elohim.
12.44: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 cried out and said, “He who believes in Me, believes not in Me but in Him who sent Me.
12.45: “And he who sees Me sees Him who sent Me.
12.46: “I have come as a Light into the world, so that no one who believes in Me should stay in darkness.
12.47: “And if anyone hears My Words but does not watch over them, I do not judge him. For I did not come to judge the world but to save the world.
12.48: “He who rejects Me, and does not receive My Words, has one who judges him: the Word that I have spoken shall judge him in the last day.
12.49: “Because I spoke not from Myself, but the Father who sent Me has given Me a Command, what I should say and what I should speak.
12.50: “And I know that His Command is everlasting ḥai. Therefore, whatever I speak, as the Father has said to Me, so I speak.”

13.1: And before the Festival of the Pesaḥ, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 knowing that His hour had come that He should move out of this world unto the Father, having loved His own who were in the world, He loved them to the end.
13.2: And supper taking place, the devil having already put it into the heart of Yahuḏah from Qeriyoth, of Shim’on, to deliver Him up,
13.3: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, knowing that the Father had given all into His hands, and that He had come from Elohim and was going to Elohim,
13.4: rose from supper and laid aside His garments, and having taken a towel, He girded Himself.
13.5: After that He put water into a basin and began to wash the feet of the talmidim, and to wipe them with the towel with which He was girded.
13.6: And so He came to Shim’on Kĕpha, and he said to Him, “Aḏonai, do You wash my feet?”
13.7: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered and said to him, “You do not know what I am doing now, but you shall know after this.”
13.8: Kĕpha said to Him, “By no means shall You wash my feet, ever!” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered him, “If I do not wash you, you have no part with Me.”
13.9: Shim’on Kĕpha said to Him, “Aḏonai, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head!”
13.10: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “He who has had a bath does not need to wash, except his feet, but is clean altogether. And you are clean, but not all of you.”
13.11: For He knew who would deliver Him up, so He said, “You are not all clean.”
13.12: So when He had washed their feet and taken His garments, and sat down again, He said to them, “Do you know what I have done to you?
13.13: “You call me Teacher and Aḏon, and you say well, for I am.
13.14: “Then if I, Aḏon and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.
13.15: “For I gave you an example, that you should do as I have done to you.
13.16: “Truly, truly, I say to you, a servant is not greater than his master, nor is an emissary greater than he who sent him.
13.17: “If you know these, ashrĕ are you if you do them.
13.18: “I do not speak concerning all of you. I know whom I have chosen, but that the Scripture might be filled, ‘He who eats bread with Me has lifted up his heel against Me.’
13.19: “Now I say to you, before it takes place, that when it does take place, you shall believe that I am.
13.20: “Truly, truly, I say to you, he who receives whomever I send, receives Me. And he who receives Me, receives Him who sent Me.”
13.21: When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had said this He was troubled in spirit, and witnessed and said, “Truly, truly, I say to you, one of you shall deliver Me up.”
13.22: The talmidim looked at one another, doubting of whom He spoke.
13.23: And one of His talmidim, whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 loved, was reclining on the bosom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
13.24: Shim’on Kĕpha then motioned to him to ask who it was of whom He spoke.
13.25: And leaning back on the breast of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 he said to Him, “Aḏonai, who is it?”
13.26: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered, “It is he to whom I shall give a piece of bread when I have dipped it.” And having dipped the bread, He gave it to Yahuḏah from Qeriyoth, of Shim’on.
13.27: And after the piece of bread, Satan entered into him. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, therefore, said to him, “What you do, do quickly.”
13.28: But no one at the table knew why He said this to him,
13.29: for some were supposing, because Yahuḏah had the bag, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was saying to him, “Buy what we need for the Festival,” or that he should give somewhat to the poor.
13.30: So, having received the piece of bread, he then went out straightaway, and it was night.
13.31: When, therefore, he went out, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said, “Now the Bĕn of Aḏam has been esteemed, and Elohim has been esteemed in Him.
13.32: “If Elohim has been esteemed in Him, Elohim shall also esteem Him in Himself, and straightaway esteem Him.
13.33: “Little children, yet a little while I am with you. You shall seek Me, and as I said to the Yahuḏim, ‘Where I am going, you are unable to come,’ I now also say to you.
13.34: “A renewed Command I give to you, that you love one another, as I have loved you, that you also love one another.
13.35: “By this shall all know that you are My talmidim, if you have love for one another.”
13.36: Shim’on Kĕpha said to Him, “Aḏonai, where are You going?” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered him, “Where I am going you are unable to follow Me now, but afterwards you shall follow Me.”
13.37: Kĕpha said to Him, “Aḏonai, why am I unable to follow You now? I shall lay down my life for You.”
13.38: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered him, “Shall you lay down your life for Me? Truly, truly, I say to you, the cock shall not crow at all until you have denied Me three times.

14.1: “Let not your heart be troubled. Believe in Elohim, believe also in Me.
14.2: “In My Father’s house are many staying places. And if not, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.
14.3: “And if I go and prepare a place for you, I shall come again and receive you to Myself, that where I am, you might be too.
14.4: “And where I go you know, and the way you know.”
14.5: T’oma said to Him, “Aḏonai, we do not know where You are going, and how are we able to know the way?”
14.6: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “I am the Way, and the Truth, and the Ḥai. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
14.7: “If you had known Me, you would have known My Father too. From now on you know Him, and have seen Him.”
14.8: Philippos said to Him, “Aḏonai, show us the Father, and it is enough for us.”
14.9: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “Have I been with you so long, and you have not known Me, Philippos? He who has seen Me has seen the Father, and how do you say, ‘Show us the Father’?
14.10: “Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in Me? The words that I speak to you I do not speak from Myself. But the Father who stays in Me does His works.
14.11: “Believe Me that I am in the Father and the Father in Me, otherwise believe Me because of the works themselves.
14.12: “Truly, truly, I say to you, he who believes in Me, the works that I do he shall do also. And greater than these he shall do, because I go to My Father.
14.13: “And whatever you ask in My Name, that I shall do, in order that the Father might be esteemed in the Bĕn.
14.14: “If you ask whatever in My Name, I shall do it.
14.15: “If you love Me, you shall guard My Commands.
14.16: “And I shall ask the Father, and He shall give you another Helper, to stay with you forever -
14.17: the Ruaḥ of the Truth, whom the world is unable to receive, because it does not see Him or know Him. But you know Him, for He stays with you and shall be in you.
14.18: “I shall not leave you orphans - I am coming to you.
14.19: “Yet a little while, and the world no longer sees Me, but you shall see Me, because I live, and you shall live.
14.20: “In that day you shall know that I am in My Father, and you in Me, and I in you.
14.21: “He who possesses My Commands and guards them, it is he who loves Me. And he who loves Me shall be loved by My Father, and I shall love him and manifest Myself to him.”
14.22: Yahuḏah - not the one from Qeriyoth - said to Him, “Aḏonai, what has come about that You are about to manifest Yourself to us, and not to the world?”
14.23: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered him, “If anyone loves Me, he shall guard My Word. And My Father shall love him, and We shall come to him and make Our stay with him.
14.24: “He who does not love Me does not guard My Words. And the Word which you hear is not Mine but of the Father who sent Me.
14.25: “These I have spoken to you while still with you.
14.26: “But the Helper, the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, whom the Father shall send in My Name, He shall teach you all, and remind you of all that I said to you.
14.27: “Peace I leave with you - My peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
14.28: “You heard that I said to you, ‘I am going away and I am coming to you.’ If you loved Me, you would have rejoiced that I said, ‘I am going to the Father,’ for My Father is greater than I.
14.29: “And now I have told you before it takes place, that when it does take place, you shall believe.
14.30: “I shall no longer talk much with you, for the ruler of this world is coming, and he possesses naught in Me,
14.31: but, in order for the world to know that I love the Father, and that as the Father commanded Me, so I am doing. Rise up, let us go from here.

15.1: “I am the true vine, and My Father is the gardener.
15.2: “Every branch in Me that bears no fruit He takes away. And every branch that bears fruit He prunes, so that it bears more fruit.
15.3: “You are already clean because of the Word which I have spoken to you.
15.4: “Stay in Me, and I in you. As the branch is unable to bear fruit of itself, unless it stays in the vine, so neither you, unless you stay in Me.
15.5: “I am the vine, you are the branches. He who stays in Me, and I in him, he bears much fruit. Because without Me you are able to do naught!
15.6: “If anyone does not stay in Me, he is thrown away as a branch and dries up. And they gather them and throw them into the fire, and they are burned.
15.7: “If you stay in Me, and My Words stay in you, you shall ask whatever you want, and it shall be done for you.
15.8: “In this My Father is esteemed, that you bear much fruit, and you shall be My talmidim.
15.9: “As the Father has loved Me, I have also loved you. Stay in My love.
15.10: “If you guard My Commands, you shall stay in My love, even as I have guarded My Father’s Commands and stay in His love.
15.11: “These I have spoken to you, so that My joy might be in you, and that your joy might be complete.
15.12: “This is My Command, that you love one another, as I have loved you.
15.13: “No one has greater love than this: that one should lay down his life for his friends.
15.14: “You are My friends if you do whatever I Command you.
15.15: “No longer do I call you servants, for a servant does not know what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, for all which I heard from My Father I have made known to you.
15.16: “You did not choose Me, but I chose you and appointed you that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in My Name He might give you.
15.17: “These I Command you, so that you love one another.
15.18: “If the world hates you, know that it hated Me before you.
15.19: “If you were of the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not of the world, yet I chose you out of the world, for that reason the world hates you.
15.20: “Remember the word that I said to you, ‘A servant is not greater than his master.’ If they persecuted Me, they shall persecute you too. If they have guarded My Word, they shall guard yours too.
15.21: “But all this they shall do to you because of My Name, because they do not know Him who sent Me.
15.22: “If I had not come and spoken to them, they would have no sin, but now they have no excuse for their sin.
15.23: “He who hates Me hates My Father as well.
15.24: “If I did not do among them the works which no one else did, they would have no sin. But now they have both seen and have hated both Me and My Father,
15.25: but that the word might be filled which was written in their Torah, ‘They hated Me without a cause.’
15.26: “And when the Helper comes, whom I shall send to you from the Father, the Ruaḥ of the Truth, who comes from the Father, He shall bear witness of Me,
15.27: but you also bear witness, because you have been with Me from the beginning.

16.1: “These I have spoken to you, so that you do not stumble.
16.2: “They shall put you out of the congregations, but an hour is coming when everyone who kills you shall think he is rendering service to Elohim.
16.3: “And this they shall do to you because they did not know the Father, nor Me.
16.4: “But I have said these to you, so that when the hour comes you remember that I told them to you. And these I did not say to you at the beginning, for I was with you.
16.5: “But now I go away to Him who sent Me, and not one of you asks Me, ‘Where are You going?’
16.6: “But because I have said these to you, grief has filled your heart.
16.7: “But I say the truth to you. It is better for you that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Helper shall not come to you at all, but if I go, I shall send Him to you.
16.8: “And having come, He shall reprove the world concerning sin, and concerning righteousness, and concerning judgment -
16.9: concerning sin because they do not believe in Me,
16.10: concerning righteousness because I go to My Father and you see Me no more,
16.11: concerning judgment because the ruler of this world is judged.
16.12: “I still have much to say to you, but you are not able to bear them now.
16.13: “But when He comes, the Ruaḥ of the Truth, He shall guide you into all the truth. For He shall not speak from Himself, but whatever He hears He shall speak, and He shall announce to you what is to come.
16.14: “He shall esteem Me, for He shall take of what is Mine and announce it to you.
16.15: “All that the Father has is Mine. That is why I said that He takes from what is Mine and shall announce it to you.
16.16: “A little while, and you do not see Me, and again a little while, and you shall see Me because I am going to the Father.”
16.17: Therefore some of His talmidim said to one another, “What is this that He says to us, ‘A little while, and you do not see Me, and again a little while, and you shall see Me,’ and, ‘because I am going to the Father’?”
16.18: So they said, “What is this that He says, ‘A little while’? We do not know what He is saying.”
16.19: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, therefore, knew that they were wanting to ask Him, and He said to them, “Are you asking one another about what I said, ‘A little while, and you do not see Me, and again a little while, and you shall see Me’?
16.20: “Truly, truly, I say to you that you shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice. And you shall be grieved, but your grief shall become joy.
16.21: “The woman has grief when she is in labor, because her hour has come, but as soon as she has given birth to the child, she no longer remembers the affliction, for joy that a man was born into the world.
16.22: “And you, therefore, have grief now, but I shall see you again and your heart shall rejoice, and no one takes your joy away from you.
16.23: “And in that day you shall ask Me naught. Truly, truly, I say to you, whatever you ask the Father in My Name He shall give you.
16.24: “Until now you have asked naught in My Name. Ask, and you shall receive, in order that your joy might be complete.
16.25: “These I have spoken to you in figures of speech, but an hour is coming when I shall no longer speak to you in figures of speech, but I shall declare to you plainly concerning the Father.
16.26: “In that day you shall ask in My Name, and I do not say to you that I shall pray the Father on your behalf,
16.27: for the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me, and have believed that I came forth from Elohim.
16.28: “I came forth from the Father and have come into the world. Again, I leave the world and go to the Father.”
16.29: His talmidim said to Him, “See, now You are speaking plainly, and not using figure of speech!
16.30: “Now we know that You know all, and have no need that anyone should question You. By this we believe that You came forth from Elohim.”
16.31: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered them, “Do you now believe?
16.32: “See, an hour is coming, and has now come, that you are scattered, each to his own, and leave Me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.
16.33: “These I have spoken to you, that in Me you might have peace. In the world you have pressure, but take courage, I have overcome the world.”

17.1: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said these, and lifted up His eyes to the shamayim, and said, “Father, the hour has come. Esteem Your Bĕn, so that Your Bĕn also might esteem You,
17.2: as You have given Him authority over all flesh, that He should give everlasting ḥai to all whom You have given Him.
17.3: “And this is everlasting ḥai, that they should know You, the only true Elohim, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 Mashiaḥ whom You have sent.
17.4: “I have esteemed You on the earth, having accomplished the work You have given Me that I should do.
17.5: “And now, esteem Me with Yourself, Father, with the esteem which I had with You before the world was.
17.6: “I have revealed Your Name to the men whom You gave Me out of the world. They were Yours, and You gave them to Me, and they have guarded Your Word.
17.7: “Now they have come to know that all You gave to Me, is from You.
17.8: “Because the Words which You gave to Me, I have given to them. And they have received them, and have truly known that I came forth from You, and they believed that You sent Me.
17.9: “I pray for them. I do not pray for the world but for those whom You have given Me, for they are Yours.
17.10: “And all Mine are Yours, and Yours are Mine, and I have been esteemed in them.
17.11: “And I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to You. Qodesh Father, guard them in Your Name which You have given Me, so that they might be one, as We are.
17.12: “When I was with them in the world, I was guarding them in Your Name which You have given Me, and I watched over them, and not one of them perished except the son of destruction, that the Scripture might be filled.
17.13: “And now I come to You. And I speak these in the world, so that they have My joy completed in them.
17.14: “I have given them Your Word, and the world hated them because they are not of the world, as I am not of the world.
17.15: “I do not pray that You should take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the wicked.
17.16: “They are not of the world, as I am not of the world.
17.17: “Qadosh them in Your truth - Your Word is truth.
17.18: “As You sent Me into the world, I also sent them into the world.
17.19: “And for them I qadosh Myself, so that they too might be qadosh in truth.
17.20: “And I do not pray for these alone, but also for those believing in Me through their word,
17.21: so that they all might be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I in You, so that they too might be one in Us, so that the world might believe that You have sent Me.
17.22: “And the esteem which You gave Me I have given them, so that they might be one as We are one,
17.23: “I in them, and You in Me, so that they might be perfected into one, so that the world knows that You have sent Me, and have loved them as You have loved Me.
17.24: “Father, I desire that those whom You have given Me, might be with Me where I am, so that they see My esteem which You have given Me, because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.
17.25: “O righteous Father, indeed the world did not know You, but I knew You, and these knew that You sent Me.
17.26: “And I have made Your Name known to them, and shall make it known, so that the love with which You loved Me might be in them, and I in them.”

18.1: Having said these, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 went out with His talmidim beyond the Qiḏron torrent, where there was a garden, into which He and His talmidim entered.
18.2: And Yahuḏah, who delivered Him up, also knew the place, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 often met there with His talmidim.
18.3: Yahuḏah, then, having received the squad and officers from the chief kohenim and Pharisees, came there with lanterns, and torches, and weapons.
18.4: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, then, knowing all that would come upon Him, went forward and said to them, “Whom do you seek?”
18.5: They answered Him, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 of Natsareth.” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “I am.” And Yahuḏah, who delivered Him up, was also standing with them.
18.6: When, therefore, He said to them, “I am,” they drew back and fell to the ground.
18.7: Once more He asked them, “Whom do you seek?” And they said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 of Natsareth.”
18.8: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered, “I said to you that I am. If, then, you seek Me, allow these to go,”
18.9: in order that the word might be filled which He spoke, “Of those whom You have given Me, I have lost none.”
18.10: Then Shim’on Kĕpha, having a sword, drew it and struck the kohĕn ha’gadol’s servant, and cut off his right ear. And the servant’s name was Meleḵ.
18.11: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to Kĕpha; “Put your sword into the sheath. Shall I not drink the cup which My Father has given Me?”
18.12: Then the squad and the commander and the officers of the Yahuḏim seized 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and bound Him,
18.13: and they led Him away to Ḥanan first, for he was the father-in-law of Qayapha who was kohĕn ha’gadol that year.
18.14: Now Qayapha was the one who gave counsel to the Yahuḏim that it was better that one man should die for the people.
18.15: And Shim’on Kĕpha followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, with another talmid, and that talmid was known to the kohĕn ha’gadol, and went with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 into the courtyard of the kohĕn ha’gadol.
18.16: But Kĕpha was standing outside at the door. So the other talmid, who was known to the kohĕn ha’gadol, went out and spoke to her who kept the door, and brought Kĕpha in.
18.17: Then the servant girl who kept the door said to Kĕpha, “Are you also one of this Man’s talmidim?” He said, “I am not.”
18.18: And the servants and officers who had made a fire of coals stood there, because it was cold, and they warmed themselves. And Kĕpha was standing with them and warming himself.
18.19: Then the kohĕn ha’gadol asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 about His talmidim and His teaching.
18.20: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered him, “I spoke openly to the world. I always taught in the congregation and in the Miqdash, where the Yahuḏim always meet, and I spoke naught in secret.
18.21: “Why do you ask Me? Ask those who have heard Me what I said to them. See, they know what I said.”
18.22: And when He had said this, one of the officers who stood by slapped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 in the face, saying, “Do You answer the kohĕn ha’gadol this way?”
18.23: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered him, “If I have spoken evilly, bear witness of the evil, but if well, why do you strike Me?”
18.24: Then Ḥanan sent Him bound to the kohĕn ha’gadol, Qayapha.
18.25: And Shim’on Kĕpha was standing and warming himself. Then they said to him, “Are you also one of His talmidim?” He denied it and said, “I am not!”
18.26: One of the servants of the kohĕn ha’gadol, a relative of the one whose ear Kĕpha cut off, said, “Did I not see you in the garden with Him?”
18.27: Then Kĕpha again denied it, and immediately a cock crowed.
18.28: Then they led 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 from Qayapha to the palace, and it was early. And they themselves did not go into the palace, lest they should be defiled, but that they might eat the Pesaḥ.
18.29: Pilatus, therefore, came out to them and said, “What accusation do you bring against this Man?”
18.30: They answered and said to him, “If He were not an evil-doer, we would not have delivered Him up to you.”
18.31: Then Pilatus said to them, “You take Him and judge Him according to your law.” The Yahuḏim said to him, “It is not right for us to put anyone to death,”
18.32: in order that the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 might be filled which He spoke, signifying by what death He was about to die.
18.33: Then Pilatus went back into the palace, and called 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, and said to Him, “You are the Meleḵ of the Yahuḏim?”
18.34: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered him, “Do you say this from yourself, or did others talk to you about Me?”
18.35: Pilatus answered, “Am I Yahuḏi? Your own nation and the chief kohenim have delivered You to me. What did You do?”
18.36: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered, “My Malḵuth is not of this world. If My Malḵuth were of this world, My servants would fight, so that I should not be delivered to the Yahuḏim. But now My Malḵuth is not from here.”
18.37: Then Pilatus said to Him, “You are a Meleḵ, then?” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered, “You say it, because I am a Meleḵ. For this I was born, and for this I have come into the world, that I should bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears My voice.”
18.38: Pilatus said to Him, “What is truth?” And when he had said this, he went out again to the Yahuḏim, and said to them, “I find no guilt in Him.
18.39: “But you have a custom that I shall release someone to you at the Pesaḥ. Do you want, then, that I release to you the Meleḵ of the Yahuḏim?”
18.40: Then they all shouted again, saying, “Not this One, but Barabba!” And Barabba was a robber.

19.1: Then, therefore, Pilatus took 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and flogged.
19.2: And the soldiers plaited a crown of thorns and placed it on His head, and they put a purple robe on Him,
19.3: and came to Him and said, “Greetings, Meleḵ of the Yahuḏim!” And they slapped Him in the face.
19.4: And Pilatus went outside again, and said to them, “See, I am bringing Him out to you, to let you know that I find no guilt in Him.”
19.5: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 came outside, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe. And Pilatus said to them, “See the Man!”
19.6: So when the chief kohenim and officers saw Him, they shouted, saying, “Impale! Impale!” Pilatus said to them, “You take Him and impale Him, for I find no guilt in Him.”
19.7: The Yahuḏim answered him, “We have a law, and according to our law He ought to die, for He has made Himself the Bĕn of Elohim.”
19.8: So when Pilatus heard this word, he was more afraid,
19.9: and went back into the palace, and asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, “Where are You from?” But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 gave him no answer.
19.10: Then Pilatus said to Him, “Do You not speak to me? Do You not know that I possess authority to impale You, and I possess authority to release You?”
19.11: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered, “You would possess no authority against Me if it were not given you from above. Because of this, he who delivered Me to you has greater sin.”
19.12: From then on Pilatus was seeking to release Him, but the Yahuḏim shouted, saying, “If you release this One, you are not Kaisar’s friend. Everyone who makes himself a meleḵ, speaks against Kaisar.”
19.13: Therefore, when Pilatus heard these words, he brought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 out and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called Pavement, but in Iḇri, Gabbatha.
19.14: And it was the Preparation of the Pesaḥ, and about the sixth hour. And he said to the Yahuḏim, “See your Meleḵ!”
19.15: But they shouted, “Away, away, impale Him!” Pilatus said to them, “Shall I impale your Meleḵ?” The chief kohenim answered, “We have no meleḵ except Kaisar!”
19.16: At that time, then, he delivered Him to them to be impaled. And they took 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and led away.
19.17: And bearing His stake, He went out to the so-called Place of a Skull, which is called in Iḇri, Golgotha,
19.18: where they impaled Him, and two others with Him, one on this side and one on that side, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 in the middle.
19.19: And Pilatus wrote a title too, and put it on the stake, and it was written: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 OF NATSARETH, THE MELEḴ OF THE YAHUḎIM.
19.20: Many of the Yahuḏim therefore read this title, for the place where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was impaled was near the city, and it was written in Iḇri, in Yawanite, in Roman.
19.21: So the chief kohenim of the Yahuḏim said to Pilatus, “Do not write, ‘The Meleḵ of the Yahuḏim,’ but, ‘He said, “I am the Meleḵ of the Yahuḏim.” ’ ”
19.22: Pilatus answered, “What I have written, I have written.”
19.23: Then the soldiers, when they had impaled 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, took His outer garments and made four parts, to each soldier a part, and the inner garment. But the inner garment was without seam, woven from the top in one piece.
19.24: So they said to each other, “Let us not tear it, but cast lots for it - whose it shall be,” in order that the Scripture might be filled which says, “They divided My garments among them, and for My clothing they cast lots.” The soldiers therefore indeed did this.
19.25: And by the stake of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 stood His mother, and His mother’s sister, Miryam the wife of Ḥĕleph, and Miryam from Maḡdala.
19.26: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, seeing His mother and the talmid whom He loved standing by, He said to His mother, “Woman, see your son!”
19.27: Then to the talmid He said, “See, your mother!” And from that hour that talmid took her to his own home.
19.28: After this, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, knowing that all had already been accomplished, in order that Scripture might be accomplished, said, “I thirst!”
19.29: A bowl full of vinegar stood there, and they filled a sponge with vinegar, put it on hyssop, and held it to His mouth.
19.30: So when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 took the vinegar He said, “It has been accomplished!” And bowing His head, He gave up His spirit.
19.31: Therefore, since it was the Preparation, that the bodies should not remain on the stake on the Shabbath - for that Shabbath was a high one - the Yahuḏim asked Pilatus to have their legs broken, and be taken away.
19.32: Therefore the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first, and of the other who was impaled with Him,
19.33: but when they came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs.
19.34: But one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and instantly blood and water came out.
19.35: And he who has seen has witnessed, and his witness is true. And he knows that he is speaking the truth, in order that you might believe.
19.36: For this took place in order for the Scripture to be filled: “Not one of His bones shall be broken.”
19.37: And again another Scripture says, “They shall look on Him whom they pierced.”
19.38: And after this, Yosĕph of Ramathayim, being a talmid of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, but secretly, for fear of the Yahuḏim, asked Pilatus that he might take the body of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, and Pilatus gave permission. Therefore he came and took the body of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
19.39: And Naḵdimon, who at first came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 by night, also came, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred litras.
19.40: Then they took the body of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, and bound it in linen wrappings with the spices, as was the habit of the Yahuḏim for burial.
19.41: And at the place where He was impaled there was a garden, and in the garden a fresh tomb in which no one had yet been laid.
19.42: There, then, because of the Preparation of the Yahuḏim, they laid 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, because the tomb was near.

2.1: And on the third day there was a wedding in Qanah of Galil, and the mother of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was there.
2.2: And both 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and His talmidim were invited to the wedding.
2.3: And when they were short of wine, the mother of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to Him, “They have no wine.”
2.4: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “Woman, what is that to Me and to you? My hour has not yet come.”
2.5: His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever He says to you.”
2.6: And there were six stone water-jugs standing there, according to the mode of cleansing of the Yahuḏim, each holding two or three metrĕtĕs.
2.7: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Fill the water­jugs with water.” And they filled them up to the brim.
2.8: And He said to them, “Now draw out and take it to the master of the feast.” So they took it.
2.9: But when the master of the feast had tasted the water that had become wine, and did not know where it came from - though the servants who had drawn the water knew - the master of the feast called the bridegroom,
2.10: and said to him, “Every man at the beginning puts out the good wine, and when they have drunk freely, then that which is poorer. You have kept the good wine until now.”
2.11: This, the beginning of the signs, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 did in Qanah of Galil, and manifested His esteem. And His talmidim believed in Him.
2.12: After this He went down to Kephar Naḥum, He and His mother, and His brothers, and His talmidim. And there they stayed not many days.
2.13: And the Pesaḥ of the Yahuḏim was near, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 went up to Yerushalayim.
2.14: And He found in the Miqdash those selling oxen and sheep and doves, and the moneychangers sitting.
2.15: And having made a whip of cords, He drove them all out of the Miqdash, with the sheep and the oxen, and poured out the moneychangers’ coins and overturned the tables.
2.16: And He said to those selling doves, “Take these away! Do not make the house of My Father a house of merchandise!”
2.17: And His talmidim remembered that it was written, “The ardor for Your house has eaten Me up.”
2.18: And the Yahuḏim answered and said to Him, “What sign do You show to us, since You are doing these?”
2.19: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered and said to them, “Destroy this Mishkan, and in three days I shall raise it.”
2.20: Then the Yahuḏim said, “It took forty-six years to build this Mishkan, and You are going to raise it in three days?”
2.21: But He spoke about the Mishkan of His body.
2.22: So, when He was raised from the dead, His talmidim remembered that He said this to them. And they believed the Scripture and the word which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had said.
2.23: And when He was in Yerushalayim at the Pesaḥ, at the Festival, many believed in His Name when they saw the signs which He was doing.
2.24: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was not entrusting Himself to them, because He knew all men,
2.25: and had no need that anyone should witness of man, for He knew what was in man.

20.1: And on one of the shabbathoth, Miryam from Maḡdala came to the tomb in the morning, when it was still dim, and saw that the stone had been removed from the tomb.
20.2: So she ran and came to Shim’on Kĕpha, and to the other talmid whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 loved, and said to them, “They have taken the Aḏon out of the tomb, and we do not know where they laid Him.”
20.3: Then Kĕpha and the other talmid went out, and they were going to the tomb,
20.4: and the two were running together, but the other, talmid outran Kĕpha and came to the tomb first.
20.5: And stooping down he saw the linen wrappings lying, but he did not go in.
20.6: Then Shim’on Kĕpha came, following him, and went into the tomb. And he saw the linen wrappings lying,
20.7: and the cloth which had been on His head, not lying with the linen wrappings, but folded up in a place by itself.
20.8: So, then, the other talmid, who came to the tomb first, also went in. And he saw and believed.
20.9: For they did not yet know the Scripture, that He has to rise again from the dead.
20.10: Therefore the talmidim went away again to their own homes.
20.11: But Miryam was standing outside by the tomb weeping. Then as she wept, she stooped down to the tomb,
20.12: and saw two messengers in white sitting, one at the head and the other at the feet, where the body of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had been laid.
20.13: And they said to her, “Woman, why do you weep?” She said to them, “Because they took away Aḏonai, and I do not know where they laid Him.”
20.14: And having said this, she turned around and saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 standing, but she did not know that it was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
20.15: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “Woman, why do you weep? Whom do you seek?” Thinking He was the gardener, she said to Him, “Aḏonai, if You have carried Him away, say to me where You put Him, and I shall take Him away.”
20.16: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “Miryam!” She turned and said to Him, “Rabboni!” which translated is, Teacher.
20.17: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “Do not hold on to Me, for I have not yet ascended to My Father. But go to My brothers and say to them, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, and to My Elohim and your Elohim.’ ”
20.18: Miryam from Maḡdala came announcing to the talmidim that she had seen the Aḏon, and that He had told her this.
20.19: When therefore it was evening on that day, one of the shabbathoth, and when the doors were shut where the talmidim met, for fear of the Yahuḏim, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 came and stood in the midst, and said to them, “Peace to you.”
20.20: And having said this, He showed them His hands and His side. The talmidim therefore rejoiced when they saw the Aḏon.
20.21: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them again, “Peace to you! As the Father has sent Me, I also send you.”
20.22: And having said this, He breathed on them, and said to them, “Receive the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh.
20.23: “If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them; if you retain the sins of any, they have been retained.”
20.24: But T’oma, called the Twin, one of the twelve, was not with them when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 came,
20.25: so the other talmidim said to him, “We have seen the Aḏon.” But he said to them, “Unless I see in His hands the mark of the nails, and put my finger into the imprint of the nails, and put my hand into His side, I shall by no means believe.”
20.26: And after eight days His talmidim were again inside, and T’oma with them. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 came, the doors having been shut, and He stood in the midst, and said, “Peace to you!”
20.27: Then He said to T’oma, “Bring your finger here, and see My hands. And bring your hand and put it into My side - and do not be unbelieving, but believing.”
20.28: And T’oma answered and said to Him, “Aḏonai and my Elohim!”
20.29: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “T’oma, because you have seen Me, you have believed. Ashrĕ are those who have not seen and have believed.”
20.30: There were indeed many other signs that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 did in the presence of His talmidim, which are not written in this book,
20.31: but these have been written so that you believe that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 is ha’Mashiaḥ, the Bĕn of Elohim, and that, believing, you might possess ḥai in His Name.

21.1: After this 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 manifested Himself again to the talmidim at the Sea of Kinnereth, and He manifested this way:
21.2: Shim’on Kĕpha, and T’oma called the Twin, and Nethan’ĕl of Qanah in Galil, and the sons of Zaḇdai, and two others of His talmidim were together.
21.3: Shim’on Kĕpha said to them, “I am going to fish.” They said to him, “We are also coming with you.” They went out and immediately entered into the boat. And that night they caught none at all.
21.4: But when it became early morning, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 stood on the beach. However, the talmidim did not know that it was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
21.5: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Children, have you any food?” They answered Him, “No.”
21.6: And He said to them, “Throw the net on the right side of the boat, and you shall find.” So they threw, and they were no longer able to draw it in because of the large number of fish.
21.7: That talmid whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 loved then said to Kĕpha, “It is the Aḏon!” Then Shim’on Kĕpha, hearing that it was the Aḏon, put on his outer garment - for he was stripped - and plunged into the sea.
21.8: And the other talmidim came in the little boat - for they were not far from land, but about two hundred pĕḵun - dragging the net with fish.
21.9: So when they had come to land, they saw a fire of coals there, and fish laid on it, and bread.
21.10: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Bring some of the fish which you have now caught.”
21.11: Shim’on Kĕpha went up and dragged the net to land, filled with one hundred and fifty-three big fish. And though there were so many, the net was not broken.
21.12: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Come, have breakfast.” And not one of the talmidim had the courage to ask Him, “Who are You?,” knowing that it was the Aḏon.
21.13: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 came and took the bread and gave it to them, and the same with the fish.
21.14: This was now the third time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was manifested to His talmidim after He was raised from the dead.
21.15: When, therefore, they had eaten breakfast, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to Shim’on Kĕpha, “Shim’on, of Yonah, do you love Me more than these?” He said to Him, “Yes, Aḏonai, You know that I love You.” He said to him, “Feed My lambs.”
21.16: He said to him again, the second time, “Shim’on, of Yonah, do you love Me?” He said to Him, “Yes, Aḏonai, You know that I love You.” He said to him, “Shepherd My sheep.”
21.17: He said to him the third time, “Shim’on, of Yonah, do you love Me?” Kĕpha was sad because He said to him the third time, “Do you love Me?” And he said to Him, “Aḏonai, You know all, You know that I love You.” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “Feed My sheep.
21.18: “Truly, truly, I say to you, when you were younger you girded yourself and walked where you wanted, but when you are old you shall stretch out your hands, and another shall gird you and bring you where you do not want.”
21.19: Now this He said, signifying by what death he would esteem Elohim. And having said this, He said to him, “Follow Me.”
21.20: And Kĕpha, turning around, saw the talmid whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 loved following, who also had leaned on His breast at the supper, and said, “Aḏonai, who is the one who is delivering You up?”
21.21: Seeing him, Kĕpha said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, “But Aḏonai, what about this one?”
21.22: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “If I want him to remain till I come, what is that to you? You follow Me.”
21.23: Therefore this word went out among the brothers that this talmid would not die. However, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 did not say to him that he would not die, but, “If I desire him to remain until I come, what is it to you?”
21.24: This is the talmid who bears witness about these, and wrote these. And we know that his witness is true.
21.25: Now there is much else that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 did. If every one of them were written down, I think that the world itself would not contain the written books. Amĕn.

3.1: And there was a man of the Pharisees, Naḵdimon was his name, a ruler of the Yahuḏim.
3.2: This one came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 by night and said to Him, “Rabbi, we know that You are a teacher come from Elohim, for no one is able to do these signs You do if Elohim is not with him.”
3.3: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered and said to him, “Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born from above, he is unable to see the Malḵuth of Elohim.”
3.4: Naḵdimon said to Him, “How is a man able to be born when he is old? Is he able to enter into his mother’s womb a second time and be born?”
3.5: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered, “Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Ruaḥ, he is unable to enter into the Malḵuth of Elohim.
3.6: “That which has been born of the flesh is flesh, and that which has been born of the Ruaḥ is spirit.
3.7: “Do not marvel that I said to you, ‘You have to be born from above.’
3.8: “The Ruaḥ breathes where it wants, and you hear the sound of it, but do not know where it comes from and where it goes. So is everyone who has been born of the Ruaḥ.”
3.9: Naḵdimon answered and said to Him, “How is it possible for this to take place?”
3.10: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered and said to him, “Are you the teacher of Yisra’ĕl, and do not know this?
3.11: “Truly, truly, I say to you, We speak what We know and witness what We have seen, and you do not receive Our witness.
3.12: “If you do not believe when I spoke to you about earthly things, how are you going to believe when I speak to you about the matters of the shamayim?
3.13: “And no one has gone up into the shamayim except He who came down from the shamayim - the Bĕn of Aḏam.
3.14: “And as Mosheh lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so the Bĕn of Aḏam has to be lifted up,
3.15: so that whoever is believing in Him should not perish but possess everlasting ḥai.
3.16: “For Elohim so loved the world that He gave His only brought-forth Bĕn, so that everyone who believes in Him should not perish but possess everlasting ḥai.
3.17: “For Elohim did not send His Bĕn into the world to judge the world, but that the world through Him might be saved.
3.18: “He who believes in Him is not judged, but he who does not believe is judged already, because he has not believed in the Name of the only brought-forth Bĕn of Elohim.
3.19: “And this is the judgment, that the Light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the Light, for their works were wicked.
3.20: “For everyone who is practicing evil hates the Light and does not come to the Light, lest his works should be exposed.
3.21: “But the one doing the truth comes to the Light, so that his works are clearly seen, that they have been wrought in Elohim.”
3.22: After this, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and His talmidim came into the land of Yahuḏah, and He remained there with them, and was immersing.
3.23: And Yoḥanan was also immersing in Ayin near Salem, because there was plenty of water there. And they were coming and were being immersed,
3.24: for Yoḥanan had not yet been put into prison.
3.25: Then a dispute arose between some of Yoḥanan’s talmidim and the Yahuḏim about cleansing,
3.26: and they came to Yoḥanan and said to him, “Rabbi, He who was with you beyond the Yardĕn, to whom you have witnessed, see, He is immersing, and all are coming to Him!”
3.27: Yoḥanan answered and said, “A man is able to receive naught unless it is given to him from the shamayim.
3.28: “You yourselves are witnesses for me that I said, ‘I am not ha’Mashiaḥ but I am sent ahead of Him.’
3.29: “He that has the bride is the bridegroom, but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly because of the voice of the bridegroom. So this joy of mine is complete.
3.30: “It is right for Him to increase, but me to decrease.
3.31: “He who comes from above is over all, he who is from the earth is of the earth and speaks of the earth. He who comes from the shamayim is over all.
3.32: “And what He has seen and heard, that He witnesses. And no one receives His witness.
3.33: “He who receives His witness has put his seal that Elohim is true.
3.34: “For He whom Elohim has sent speaks the Words of Elohim, for Elohim does not give the Ruaḥ by measure.
3.35: “The Father loves the Bĕn, and has given all into His hand.
3.36: “He who believes in the Bĕn possesses everlasting ḥai, but he who does not obey the Bĕn shall not see ḥai, but the wrath of Elohim remains on him.”

4.1: So when the Aḏon knew that the Pharisees had heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 made and immersed more talmidim than Yoḥanan -
4.2: although 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 Himself did not immerse, but His talmidim -
4.3: He left Yahuḏah and went away again to Galil.
4.4: And He had to pass through Shomeron.
4.5: So He came to a city of Shomeron, called Syḵar, near the piece of land Ya’aqoḇ gave to his son Yosĕph.
4.6: And Ya’aqoḇ’s fountain was there. So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, being wearied from the journey, was sitting there at the fountain. It was about the sixth hour.
4.7: A woman of Shomeron came to draw water. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “Give Me to drink.”
4.8: For His talmidim had gone off into the city to buy food.
4.9: The woman of Shomeron therefore said to Him, “How is it that You, being a Yahuḏi, ask a drink from me, a woman of Shomeron?” For Yahuḏim do not associate with Shomeronites.
4.10: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered and said to her, “If you knew the gift of Elohim, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give Me to drink,’ you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.”
4.11: The woman said to Him, “Aḏonai, You have no vessel, and the well is deep. From where, then, do You have living water?
4.12: “Are You greater than our father Ya’aqoḇ, who gave us the well, and drank from it himself, and his sons, and his stock?”
4.13: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered and said to her, “Everyone drinking of this water shall thirst again,
4.14: but whoever drinks of the water I give him shall certainly never thirst. And the water that I give him shall become in him a fountain of water springing up into everlasting ḥai.”
4.15: The woman said to Him, “Aḏonai, give me this water, so that I do not thirst, nor come here to draw.”
4.16: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “Go, call your husband, and come here.”
4.17: The woman answered and said, “I have no husband.” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “You have well said, ‘I have no husband,’
4.18: for you have had five husbands, and the one whom you now have is not your husband. What you have said is true.”
4.19: The woman said to Him, “Aḏonai, I see that You are a naḇi.
4.20: “Our fathers worshipped on this mountain, but you say that in Yerushalayim is the place where one needs to worship.”
4.21: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “Woman, believe Me, the hour is coming when you shall neither on this mountain, nor in Yerushalayim, worship the Father.
4.22: “You worship what you do not know. We worship what we know, because the deliverance is of the Yahuḏim.
4.23: “But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father also seeks such to worship Him.
4.24: “Elohim is Ruaḥ, and those who worship Him need to worship in spirit and truth.”
4.25: The woman said to Him, “I know that Mashiaḥ is coming, the One who is called Anointed. When that One comes, He shall announce to us all.”
4.26: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “I who am speaking to you am He.”
4.27: And upon this His talmidim came, and they were marveling that He was speaking with a woman, however, no one said, “What do You seek?” or, “Why do You speak with her?”
4.28: The woman then left her water-jug, and went away to the city, and said to the men,
4.29: “Come, see a Man who told me all that I have done. Is this not ha’Mashiaḥ?”
4.30: They went out of the city and were coming to Him.
4.31: But in the meantime His talmidim were asking Him, saying, “Rabbi, eat.”
4.32: And He said to them, “I have food to eat of which you do not know.”
4.33: Then the talmidim said to each other, “Did anyone bring Him something to eat?”
4.34: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “My food is to do the desire of Him who sent Me, and to accomplish His work.
4.35: “Do you not say, ‘There are still four months, and the harvest comes’? See, I say to you, lift up your eyes and see the fields, for they are white for harvest - already!
4.36: “He who is reaping receives a reward, and gathers fruit for everlasting ḥai, so that both he who is sowing and he who is reaping rejoice together.
4.37: “For in this the word is true, ‘One sows and another reaps.’
4.38: “I sent you to reap that for which you have not labored. Others have labored, and you have entered into their labors.”
4.39: And many of the Shomeronites of that city believed in Him because of the word of the woman who witnessed, “He told me all that I have done.”
4.40: Therefore when the Shomeronites came to Him, they were asking Him to stay with them, and He stayed there two days.
4.41: And many more believed because of His word.
4.42: And they said to the woman, “We no longer believe because of what you said, for we ourselves have heard, and we know that this is truly ha’Mashiaḥ, the Savior of the world.”
4.43: And after the two days He left there and went to Galil.
4.44: For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 Himself witnessed that a naḇi is without appreciation in his own country.
4.45: Therefore when He came to Galil, the Galileans received Him, having seen all that He had done in Yerushalayim at the Festival, for they also went to the Festival.
4.46: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 came again to Qanah of Galil where He had made the water wine. And there was a certain nobleman whose son was sick at Kephar Naḥum.
4.47: When he heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had come from Yahuḏah into Galil, he went to Him and was asking Him to come down and heal his son, for he was about to die.
4.48: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 then said to him, “If you do not see signs and wonders, you shall not believe at all.”
4.49: The nobleman said to Him, “Aḏonai, come down before my child dies!”
4.50: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “Go, your son lives.” And the man believed the word that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 spoke to him, and went.
4.51: And while he was going down, his servants met him and reported, saying, “Your son lives!”
4.52: He then asked from them the hour in which he became better, and they said to him, “Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.”
4.53: Then the father knew that it was at the same hour in which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “Your son lives.” And he himself believed, and all his household.
4.54: Again this was the second sign 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 did, when He had come from Yahuḏah into Galil.

5.1: After this there was a Festival of the Yahuḏim, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 went up to Yerushalayim.
5.2: And in Yerushalayim at the Sheep Gate there is a pool, which is called in Iḇri, Bĕyth Zatha, having five porches.
5.3: In these were lying a great number of those who were sick, blind, crippled, paralyzed, waiting for the stirring of the water.
5.4: For a messenger was going down at a certain time into the pool and was stirring the water. Whoever stepped in first, then, after the stirring of the water, became well of whatever disease he had.
5.5: And a certain man was there who had a sickness thirty-eight years.
5.6: When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 saw him lying there, and knowing that he already had been a long time, He said to him, “Do you want to become well?”
5.7: The sick man answered Him, “Aḏonai, I have no man to put me into the pool when the water is stirred, but while I am coming, another steps down before me.”
5.8: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “Rise, take up your bed and walk.”
5.9: And immediately the man became well, and he took up his bed and was walking. Now it was Shabbath on that day.
5.10: The Yahuḏim therefore said to him who had been healed, “It is the Shabbath, it is not right for you to take up the bed.”
5.11: He answered them, “He who made me well said to me, ‘Take up your bed and walk.’ ”
5.12: Therefore they asked him, “Who is the Man who said to you, ‘Take up your bed and walk’?”
5.13: But the one who was healed did not know who it was, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had moved away, a crowd being in that place.
5.14: Afterward 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 found him in the Miqdash, and said to him, “See, you have been made well. Sin no more, so that no worse befalls you.”
5.15: The man went away, and told the Yahuḏim that it was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 who made him well.
5.16: And because of this the Yahuḏim persecuted 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, and were seeking to kill Him, because He was doing these on the Shabbath.
5.17: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered them, “My Father works until now, and I work.”
5.18: Because of this, then, the Yahuḏim were seeking all the more to kill Him, ‘because not only was He breaking the Shabbath, but He also called Elohim His own Father, making Himself equal with Elohim.’
5.19: Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 responded and said to them, “Truly, truly, I say to you, the Bĕn is able to do naught by Himself, but only that which He sees the Father doing, because whatever He does, the Bĕn also does likewise.
5.20: “For the Father loves the Bĕn, and shows Him all that He Himself does. And greater works than these He is going to show Him, in order that you marvel.
5.21: “For as the Father raises the dead and makes alive, even so the Bĕn makes alive whom He wants.
5.22: “For the Father judges no one, but has given all the judgment to the Bĕn,
5.23: that all should value the Bĕn even as they value the Father. He who does not value the Bĕn does not value the Father who sent Him.
5.24: “Truly, truly, I say to you, he who hears My Word and believes in Him who sent Me possesses everlasting ḥai, and does not come into judgment, but has passed from death into ḥai.
5.25: “Truly, truly, I say to you, the hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Bĕn of Elohim. And those having heard shall live.
5.26: “For as the Father possesses ḥai in Himself, so He gave also to the Bĕn to possess ḥai in Himself,
5.27: and He has given Him authority also to do judgment, because He is the Bĕn of Aḏam.
5.28: “Do not marvel at this, because the hour is coming in which all those in the tombs shall hear His voice,
5.29: and shall come forth - those who have done good, to the resurrection of ḥai, and those who have practiced evil, to a resurrection of judgment.
5.30: “Of Myself I am able to do naught. As I hear, I judge, and My judgment is righteous, because I do not seek My own desire, but the desire of the Father who sent Me.
5.31: “If I bear witness of Myself, My witness is not true.
5.32: “There is another who bears witness of Me, and I know that the witness which He witnesses of Me is true.
5.33: “You have sent to Yoḥanan, and he bore witness to the truth.
5.34: “But I do not receive witness from man, but I say this in order that you might be saved.
5.35: “He was the burning and shining lamp, and for a while you wanted to rejoice in his light.
5.36: “But I have a greater witness than that of Yoḥanan, for the works that the Father gave Me to accomplish, the works that I do, bear witness of Me, that the Father has sent Me.
5.37: “And the Father who sent Me, He bore witness of Me. You have neither heard His voice at any time, nor seen His form.
5.38: “And you do not have His Word staying in you, because you do not believe Him whom He sent.
5.39: “You search the Scriptures, because you think you possess everlasting ḥai in them. And these are the ones that bear witness of Me.
5.40: “But you do not desire to come to Me in order to possess ḥai.
5.41: “I do not receive esteem from men,
5.42: but I know you, that you do not have the love of Elohim in you.
5.43: “I have come in My Father’s Name and you do not receive Me, if another comes in his own name, him you shall receive.
5.44: “How are you able to believe, when you are receiving esteem from one another, and the esteem that is from the only Elohim you do not seek?
5.45: “Do not think that I shall accuse you to the Father. There is one who accuses you: Mosheh, in whom you have put your expectation.
5.46: “For if you believed Mosheh, you would have believed Me, since he wrote about Me.
5.47: “But if you do not believe his writings, how shall you believe My Words?”

6.1: After this 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 went away to the other side of the Sea of Galil, that is Lake Kinnereth.
6.2: And a large crowd was following Him, because they saw His signs which He did on those who were sick.
6.3: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 went up on a mountain, and there He sat down with His talmidim.
6.4: And the Pesaḥ was near, the Festival of the Yahuḏim.
6.5: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, lifting up His eyes and seeing a large crowd coming toward Him, said to Philippos, “Where shall we buy bread for them to eat?”
6.6: And this He said, trying him, for He Himself knew what He would do.
6.7: Philippos answered Him, “Two hundred pieces of silver worth of bread is not sufficient for them, for every one of them to receive a little.”
6.8: One of His talmidim, Andri, the brother of Shim’on Kĕpha, said to Him,
6.9: “Here is a boy who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these for so many?”
6.10: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said, “Make the people sit down.” Now there was much grass in the place, and the men, numbering about five thousand, sat down.
6.11: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 took the loaves, and having given thanks He distributed them to the talmidim, and the talmidim; to those sitting down. And the same with the fish, as much as they wanted.
