6.12: And when they were filled, He said to His talmidim, “Gather the broken pieces that are left over, so that none gets wasted.”
6.13: So they gathered them and filled twelve baskets with broken pieces of the five barley loaves which were left over by those who had eaten.
6.14: Then the men, having seen the sign that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 did, said, “This is truly the Naḇi who is coming to the world.”
6.15: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, knowing that they were about to come and seize Him, that they might make Him meleḵ, withdrew again to the mountain, alone by Himself.
6.16: And when evening came, His talmidim went down to the sea,
6.17: and entering into the boat, they were going over the sea toward Kephar Naḥum. And it had already become dark, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had not yet come to them.
6.18: And the sea was rising because a great wind was blowing.
6.19: When they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadios, they saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 walking on the sea and coming near the boat, and they were afraid.
6.20: And He said to them, “It is I, do not be afraid.”
6.21: They determined therefore to take Him into the boat, and at once the boat was at the land where they were going.
6.22: On the next day, the crowd that was standing on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there except that one into which His talmidim had entered, and that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had not entered the boat with His talmidim, but His talmidim went away alone -
6.23: but other boats came from Tiberias, near the place where they ate bread after the Aḏon had given thanks -
6.24: therefore when the crowd saw that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was not there, nor His talmidim, they themselves also entered into the boats and came to Kephar Naḥum, seeking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
6.25: And having found Him on the other side of the sea, they asked Him, “Rabbi, when did You come here?”
6.26: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered them and said, “Truly, truly, I say to you, you seek Me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were satisfied.
6.27: “Do not labor for the food that is perishing, but for the food that is remaining to everlasting ḥai, which the Bĕn of Aḏam shall give you, for the Father, Elohim, has put His seal on Him.”
6.28: So they said to Him, “What should we do to work the works of Elohim?”
6.29: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered and said to them, “This is the work of Elohim, that you believe in Him whom He sent.”
6.30: So they said to Him, “What sign then would You do, so that we see and believe You? What would You do?
6.31: “Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, as it has been written, ‘He gave them bread out of the shamayim to eat.’ ”
6.32: Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Truly, truly, I say to you, Mosheh did not give you the bread out of the shamayim, but My Father gives you the true bread out of the shamayim.
6.33: “For the bread of Elohim is He who comes down out of the shamayim and gives Ḥai to the world.”
6.34: So they said to Him, “Aḏonai, give us this bread always.”
6.35: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “I am the bread of Ḥai. He who comes to Me shall not get hungry at all, and he who believes in Me shall not get thirsty at all.
6.36: “But I said to you that you have seen Me, and still do not believe.
6.37: “All that the Father gives Me shall come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I shall by no means cast out.
6.38: “Because I have come down out of the shamayim, not to do My own desire, but the desire of Him who sent Me.
6.39: “This is the desire of the Father who sent Me, that all He has given Me I should not lose of it, but should raise it in the last day.
6.40: “And this is the desire of Him who sent Me, that everyone who sees the Bĕn and believes in Him should possess everlasting ḥai. And I shall raise him up in the last day.”
6.41: Therefore the Yahuḏim were grumbling against Him, because He said, “I am the bread which came down out of the shamayim.”
6.42: And they said, “Is not this 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, the son of Yosĕph, whose father and mother we know? How is it then that He says, ‘I have come down out of the shamayim’?”
6.43: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered and said to them, “Do not grumble with one another.
6.44: “No one is able to come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him. And I shall raise him up in the last day.
6.45: “It has been written in the Neḇi’im, ‘And they shall all be taught by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’ Everyone, then, who has heard from the Father, and learned, comes to Me.
6.46: “Not that anyone has seen the Father, except He who is from Elohim - He has seen the Father.
6.47: “Truly, truly, I say to you, he who believes in Me possesses everlasting ḥai.
6.49: “Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and they died.
6.50: “This is the bread which comes down out of the shamayim, so that anyone might eat of it, and not die.
6.51: “I am the living bread which came down out of the shamayim. If anyone eats of this bread, he shall live forever. And indeed, the bread that I shall give is My flesh, which I shall give for the ḥai of the world.”
6.52: The Yahuḏim, therefore, were striving with one another, saying, “How is this One able to give us flesh to eat?”
6.53: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 therefore said to them, “Truly, truly, I say to you, unless you eat the flesh of the Bĕn of Aḏam and drink His blood, you possess no ḥai in yourselves.
6.54: “He who eats My flesh and drinks My blood possesses everlasting ḥai, and I shall raise him up in the last day.
6.55: “For My flesh is truly food, and My blood is truly drink.
6.56: “He who eats My flesh and drinks My blood stays in Me, and I in him.
6.57: “As the living Father sent Me, and I live because of the Father, so he who feeds on Me shall live because of Me.
6.58: “This is the bread which came down out of the shamayim, not as your fathers ate the manna and died. He who eats this bread shall live forever.”
6.59: He said this in a congregation, teaching in Kephar Naḥum.
6.60: Therefore many of His talmidim having heard, said, “This word is hard, who is able to hear it?”
6.61: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 knowing within Himself that His talmidim were grumbling about this, said to them, “Does this make you stumble?
6.62: “What if you see the Bĕn of Aḏam going up where He was before?
6.63: “It is the Ruaḥ, that gives ḥai, the flesh does not profit at all. The words that I speak to you are Ruaḥ and are ḥai.
6.64: “But there are some of you who do not believe.” For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 knew from the beginning who they were who did not believe, and who would deliver Him up.
6.65: And He said, “Because of this I have said to you that no one is able to come to Me unless it has been given to him by My Father.”
6.66: From then on many of His talmidim withdrew and were not walking with Him anymore.
6.67: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 therefore said to the twelve, “Do you also want to go away?”
6.68: Then Shim’on Kĕpha answered Him, “Aḏonai, to whom shall we go? You possess words of everlasting ḥai.
6.69: “And we have believed, and we know that You are ha’Mashiaḥ, the Bĕn of the living Elohim.”
6.70: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered them, “Have I not chosen you, the twelve, and one of you is a devil?”
6.71: He was now speaking of Yahuḏah from Qeriyoth, of Shim’on, for he, one of the twelve, was about to deliver Him up.

7.1: And after this 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was walking in Galil, for He did not want to walk in Yahuḏah, because the Yahuḏim were seeking to kill Him.
7.2: And the Festival of the Yahuḏim was near, the Festival of Sukkoth.
7.3: So His brothers said to Him, “Get away from here and go into Yahuḏah, so that Your talmidim also see the works that You are doing.
7.4: “For no one acts in secret while he himself seeks to be known openly. If You do these, show Yourself to the world.”
7.5: For even His brothers did not believe in Him.
7.6: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 therefore said to them, “My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.
7.7: “It is impossible for the world to hate you, but it hates Me because I bear witness of it, that its works are wicked.
7.8: “You go up to this Festival. I am not yet going up to this Festival, for My time has not yet been filled.”
7.9: And having said this to them, He stayed in Galil.
7.10: But when His brothers had gone up to the Festival, then He also went up, not openly, but as it were in secret.
7.11: The Yahuḏim, therefore, were seeking Him at the Festival, and said, “Where is He?”
7.12: And there was much grumbling about Him among the crowd. Some were saying, “He is good,” but others were saying, “No, but He is leading the crowd astray.”
7.13: However, no one spoke openly of Him for fear of the Yahuḏim.
7.14: And about the middle of the Festival 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 went up into the Miqdash, and He was teaching.
7.15: And the Yahuḏim were marveling, saying, “How does this Man know letters, not having learned?”
7.16: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered them and said, “My teaching is not Mine, but His who sent Me.
7.17: “If anyone desires to do His desire, he shall know concerning the teaching, whether it is from Elohim, or I speak from Myself.
7.18: “He who speaks from himself is seeking his own esteem, but He who seeks the esteem of the One who sent Him is true, and no unrighteousness is in Him.
7.19: “Did not Mosheh give you the Torah? Yet not one of you does the Torah! Why do you seek to kill Me?”
7.20: The crowd answered and said, “You have a demon, who seeks to kill You?”
7.21: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered and said to them, “I did one work, and you all marvel.
7.22: “Because of this Mosheh has given you the circumcision - though it is not from Mosheh, but from the fathers - and you circumcise a man on the Shabbath.
7.23: “If a man receives circumcision on the Shabbath, so that the Torah of Mosheh should not be broken, are you wroth with Me because I made a man entirely well on the Shabbath?
7.24: “Do not judge according to appearance, but judge with righteous judgment.”
7.25: Therefore some of them from Yerushalayim said, “Is this not He whom they are seeking to kill?
7.26: “And see! He speaks boldly, and they say none at all to Him. Could it be that the rulers truly know that this is truly ha’Mashiaḥ?
7.27: “But we know where this One is from. And when ha’Mashiaḥ comes no one knows where He is from.”
7.28: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 therefore cried out in the Miqdash, teaching and saying, “You both know Me, and you know where I am from. And I have not come of Myself, but He who sent Me is true, whom you do not know.
7.29: “But I know Him, because I am from Him, and He sent Me.”
7.30: So they were seeking to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come.
7.31: And many of the crowd believed in Him, and said, “When ha’Mashiaḥ comes, shall He do more signs than these which this One did?”
7.32: The Pharisees heard the crowd muttering these concerning Him, and the Pharisees and the chief kohenim sent officers to seize Him.
7.33: Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Yet a little while I am with you, then I go to Him who sent Me.
7.34: “You shall seek Me and you shall not find, and where I am you are unable to come.”
7.35: The Yahuḏim, therefore, said to themselves, “Where is He about to go that we shall not find Him? Is He about to go to the Dispersion among the Yawanites, and to teach the Yawanites?
7.36: “What is this word which He said, ‘You shall seek Me and you shall not find, and where I am you are unable to come’?”
7.37: And on the last Great Day of the Festival, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 stood and cried out, saying, “If anyone thirsts, let him come to Me, and let him who believes in Me drink.
7.38: “As the Scripture said, out of His innermost shall flow rivers of living water.”
7.39: And this He said concerning the Ruaḥ, which those believing in Him were about to receive, for the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh was not yet, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was not yet esteemed.
7.40: Many from the crowd, when they heard the word, then said, “This truly is the Naḇi.”
7.41: Others said, “This is ha’Mashiaḥ,” but others said, “Does ha’Mashiaḥ then come out of Galil?
7.42: “Did not the Scripture say that ha’Mashiaḥ comes from the seed of Dawiḏ and from the village of Bĕyth Leḥem, where Dawiḏ was?”
7.43: So a division came about among the people because of Him.
7.44: And some of them wanted to take Him, but no one laid hands on Him.
7.45: The officers therefore came to the chief kohenim and Pharisees. And they said to them, “Why did you not bring Him?”
7.46: The officers answered, “Never has any man spoken like this Man!”
7.47: The Pharisees, therefore, answered them, “Have you also been led astray?
7.48: “Has anyone of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed in Him?
7.49: “But this crowd that does not know the Torah is accursed.”
7.50: Naḵdimon - he who came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 by night, being one of them - said to them,
7.51: “Does our Torah judge the man unless it hears first from him and knows what he is doing?”
7.52: They answered and said to him, “Are you also from Galil? Search and see that no naḇi has arisen out of Galil.”
7.53: And each one went to his own house.

8.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 went to the Mount of Olives.
8.2: And at dawn He came again into the Miqdash, and all the people were coming to Him. And having sat down, He was teaching them.
8.3: And the scribes and Pharisees brought to Him a woman caught in adultery. And having put her in the midst,
8.4: they said to Him, “Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of adultery.
8.5: “And in the Torah Mosheh commanded us that such should be stoned. What then do You say?”
8.6: And this they said, trying Him, so that they might accuse Him. But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, bending down, wrote on the ground with the finger, as though He did not hear.
8.7: But as they kept on questioning Him, He straightened up and said to them, “He who is without sin among you, let him be the first to throw a stone at her.”
8.8: And bending down again, He wrote on the ground.
8.9: And when they heard it, being reproved by conscience, went out one by one, beginning from the older ones until the last. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was left alone, and the woman standing in the middle.
8.10: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, straightening up and seeing no one but the woman, said to her, “Woman, where are those accusers of yours? Did no one condemn you?”
8.11: And she said, “No one, Aḏonai.” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “Neither do I condemn you. Go and sin no more.”
8.12: Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 spoke to them again, saying, “I am the Light of the world. He who follows Me shall by no means walk in darkness, but possess the light of ḥai.”
8.13: The Pharisees, therefore, said to Him, “You bear witness about Yourself, Your witness is not true.”
8.14: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered and said to them, “Even if I witness concerning Myself, My witness is true, for I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know from where I come, or where I go.
8.15: “You judge according to the flesh, I judge no one.
8.16: “But even if I do judge, My judgment is true, because I am not alone, but I and the Father who sent Me.
8.17: “And in your Torah also, it has been written that the witness of two men is true.
8.18: “I am One who witnesses concerning Myself, and the Father who sent Me witnesses concerning Me.”
8.19: Therefore they said to Him, “Where is Your Father?” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered, “You know neither Me nor My Father. If you knew Me, you would have known My Father also.”
8.20: These words 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 spoke in the treasury, teaching in the Miqdash. And no one laid hands on Him, because His hour had not yet come.
8.21: Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them again, “I am going away, and you shall seek Me, and you shall die in your sin. Where I go you are unable to come.”
8.22: Then the Yahuḏim said, “Shall He kill Himself, because He says, ‘Where I go you are unable to come’?”
8.23: And He said to them, “You are from below, I am from above. You are of this world, I am not of this world.
8.24: “Therefore I said to you that you shall die in your sins. For if you do not believe that I am, you shall die in your sins.”
8.25: Then they said to Him, “Who are You?” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Altogether that which I even say to you!
8.26: “I have much to say and to judge concerning you. But He who sent Me is true, and what I heard from Him, these I speak to the world.”
8.27: They did not know that He spoke to them of the Father.
8.28: So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “When you lift up the Bĕn of Aḏam, then you shall know that I am He, and that I do naught of Myself, but as My Father taught Me, these I speak.
8.29: “And He who sent Me is with Me. The Father has not left Me alone, for I always do what pleases Him.”
8.30: As He was speaking these words, many believed in Him.
8.31: So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to those Yahuḏim who believed Him, “If you stay in My Word, you are truly My talmidim,
8.32: “and you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.”
8.33: They answered Him, “We are the seed of Aḇraham, and have been servants to no one at any time. How do you say, ‘You shall become free’?”
8.34: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered them, “Truly, truly, I say to you, everyone doing sin is a servant of sin.
8.35: “And the servant does not stay in the house forever - a son stays forever.
8.36: “If, then, the Bĕn makes you free, you shall be free indeed.
8.37: “I know that you are the seed of Aḇraham, but you seek to kill Me, because My Word has no place in you.
8.38: “I speak what I have seen with My Father, and you do what you have heard from your father.”
8.39: They answered and said to Him, “Aḇraham is our father.” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “If you were Aḇraham’s children, you would do the works of Aḇraham.
8.40: “But now you seek to kill Me, a Man who has spoken to you the truth which I heard from Elohim. Aḇraham did not do this.
8.41: “You do the works of your father.” Then they said to Him, “We were not born of whoring, we have one Father: Elohim.”
8.42: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “If Elohim were your Father, you would love Me, for I came forth from Elohim, and am here. For I have not come of Myself, but He sent Me.
8.43: “Why do you not know what I say? Because you are unable to hear My Word.
8.44: “You are of your father the devil, and the desires of your father you want to do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and has not stood in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks the lie, he speaks of his own, for he is a liar and the father of it.
8.45: “And because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me.
8.46: “Who of you proves Me wrong concerning sin? And if I speak the truth, why do you not believe Me?
8.47: “He who is of Elohim hears the Words of Elohim, therefore you do not hear because you are not of Elohim.”
8.48: The Yahuḏim answered and said to Him, “Do we not say well that You are a Shomeronite and have a demon?”
8.49: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered, “I do not have a demon, but I value My Father, and you do not value Me.
8.50: “And I do not seek My own esteem, there is One who is seeking and is judging.
8.51: “Truly, truly, I say to you, if anyone guards My Word he shall never see death at all.”
8.52: The Yahuḏim said to Him, “Now we know that You have a demon! Aḇraham died, and the neḇi’im. And You say, ‘If anyone guards My Word he shall never taste death at all.’
8.53: “Are You greater than our father Aḇraham, who died? And the neḇi’im died. Whom do You make Yourself?”
8.54: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered, “If I esteem Myself, My esteem is none at all. It is My Father who esteems Me, of whom you say that He is your Elohim.
8.55: “And you have not known Him, but I know Him. And if I say, ‘I do not know Him,’ I shall be like you, a liar. But I do know Him and I guard His Word.
8.56: “Your father Aḇraham was glad that he should see My day, and he saw it and rejoiced.”
8.57: The Yahuḏim, therefore, said to Him, “You are not yet fifty years old, and have You seen Aḇraham?”
8.58: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Truly, truly, I say to you, before Aḇraham came to be, I am.”
8.59: Therefore they picked up stones to throw at Him, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was hidden and went out of the Miqdash, going through the midst of them, and so passed by.

9.1: And passing by, He saw a man, blind from birth.
9.2: And His talmidim asked Him, saying, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he should be born blind?”
9.3: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but that the works of Elohim might be made manifest in him.
9.4: “It is necessary for Me to work the works of Him who sent Me while it is day - night is coming, when no one is able to work.
9.5: “While I am in the world, I am the Light of the world.”
9.6: Having said this, He spat on the ground and made clay with the saliva, and applied the clay to the eyes of the blind man.
9.7: And He said to him, “Go, wash in the pool of Shiloaḥ,” which translated is, sent. So he went and washed, and came seeing.
9.8: Therefore the neighbors and those who saw him before, that he was blind, said, “Is this not he who was sitting and begging?”
9.9: Others said, “This is he.” Others, “He is like him.” He said, “I am.”
9.10: So they said to him, “How were your eyes opened?”
9.11: He answered and said, “A Man called 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 made clay and applied it to my eyes and said to me, ‘Go to the pool of Shiloaḥ and wash.’ And I went and washed, and I received sight.”
9.12: And they said to him, “Where is He?” He said, “I do not know.”
9.13: They brought to the Pharisees the one who was once blind.
9.14: Now it was a Shabbath when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 made the clay and opened his eyes.
9.15: Therefore the Pharisees also asked him again how he had received his sight. He said to them, “He put clay on my eyes, and I washed, and I see.”
9.16: Therefore some of the Pharisees said, “This Man is not from Elohim, because He does not guard the Shabbath.” Others said, “How is a man who is a sinner able to do such miracles?” And there was a division among them.
9.17: So they said to the blind one again, “What do you say about Him because He opened your eyes?” And he said, “He is a naḇi.”
9.18: However, the Yahuḏim did not believe concerning him, that he had been blind and received his sight, till they called the parents of him who had received his sight.
9.19: And they asked them, saying, “Is this your son, who you say was born blind? How then does he now see?”
9.20: His parents answered them and said, “We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind,
9.21: but how he now sees we do not know, or who opened his eyes we do not know. He is of age, ask him, he shall speak concerning himself.”
9.22: His parents said this because they were afraid of the Yahuḏim, for the Yahuḏim had already agreed that if anyone confessed that He was Mashiaḥ, he should be put out of the congregation.
9.23: Because of this his parents said, “He is of age, ask him.”
9.24: So for the second time they called the man who was blind, and said to him, “Give esteem to Elohim, we know that this Man is a sinner.”
9.25: Then he answered and said, “Whether He is a sinner, I do not know. I only know that I was blind, now I see.”
9.26: And they asked him once more, “What did He do to you? How did He open your eyes?”
9.27: He answered them, “I have told you already, and you did not hear. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you want to become His talmidim too?”
9.28: Then they abused him and said, “You are His talmid, but we are talmidim of Mosheh.
9.29: “We know that Elohim has spoken to Mosheh, but this One, we do not know where He is from.”
9.30: The man answered and said to them, “Why, this is a wonder! You do not know where He is from, yet He opened my eyes!
9.31: “And we know that Elohim does not hear sinners. But if anyone reveres Elohim and does His desire, He hears him.
9.32: “From of old it has never been heard that anyone opened the eyes of one who was born blind.
9.33: “If this One were not from Elohim, He could have done naught.”
9.34: They answered and said to him, “You were completely born in sins - and are you teaching us?” And they cast him out.
9.35: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 heard that they had cast him out, and when He had found him, He said to him, “Do you believe in the Bĕn of Elohim?”
9.36: He answered and said, “Who is He, Aḏonai, that I might believe in Him?”
9.37: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “You have both seen Him and He who speaks with you is He.”
9.38: And he said, “Aḏonai, I believe,” and bowed before Him.
9.39: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said, “For judgment I have come into this world, that those not seeing might see, and those seeing might become blind.”
9.40: And those of the Pharisees who were with Him heard these words, and said to Him, “Are we blind, too?”
9.41: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “If you were blind, you would have no sin, but now you say, ‘We see,’ therefore your sin remains.
